parsed.why: Courts safeguard vulnerable detainees, but prison placement remains unresolved; official hostility and high trans-targeted harassment coexist with functional hate-crime enforcement and no trans-specific criminal ban.

Total-control repression leaves no civil space; undefined obscenity powers, official denial, forced concealment and dated execution testimony extrapolate to catastrophic state violence if a visitor is outed.
No criminal ban, bathroom access protected, courts punish attacks, and official support offset persistent social avoidance; strong rule of law sharply limits consequences for an outed visitor.
Legal split still carries criminal morality provisions; police arrest/torture queer people, official bans and no protections or recourse make thin data imply severe traveler exposure.
Gender-identity nullity, unequal age-consent law, cancelled queer events, rejection of violence protections, older anti-trans attacks and pervasive concealment indicate high social-state risk.
